title: Simulating Surveys for ELT-MOSAIC: Status of the MOSAIC Science Case after Phase A
extended_summary:
This paper presents the consolidated science case for the MOSAIC multi-object spectrograph concept on the European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). Rather than evaluating an educational intervention, it describes the scientific goals, instrument requirements, and survey strategies developed during the MOSAIC Phase A study, using simulations to assess feasibility and optimize design trade-offs.

The approach centers on end-to-end scientific simulations with the WEBSIM-COMPASS tool to estimate observing times, signal-to-noise requirements, and survey speed for proposed MOSAIC programmes. The paper outlines four high-priority extragalactic survey themes: mass assembly and evolution of dwarf galaxies, inventory of matter, first-light galaxies and reionisation, and extragalactic stellar populations. It also discusses observational modes such as high-definition IFUs, visible IFUs, and high-multiplex near-IR and visible modes.

The relevant population/context here is astronomical targets such as distant galaxies, intergalactic gas, circumgalactic gas, and resolved stellar populations in nearby galaxies, observed with future ELT instrumentation. The main conclusion is that MOSAIC’s Phase A design can support a broad and transformational extragalactic science programme, though some science cases are limited by wavelength coverage and performance constraints. The paper argues that multiplex, throughput, and spectral resolution are key determinants of survey efficiency and that MOSAIC will be competitive with other future facilities for many of the highlighted programmes.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a conceptual/survey-design proceedings article about the MOSAIC astronomical instrument and its simulated science cases, not an educational intervention study. It contains no K-12 education methodology, no student-level empirical comparison, and no direct evidence relevant to Khanmigo or science learning outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no observed educational impact because the paper does not evaluate any instructional technology in schools or measure student learning outcomes. The content is unrelated to K-12 science learning and provides no evidence of effect.
